evidence: Every one of the 28 criteria (16 functional, 6 polish, 4 visual likert, 2 gates) was read in full. Each binary criterion names concrete in-browser actions with distinctive JUDGE-* probes and checks a durable readback, never just a response shape: reload or a second context (nested_replies leg 3, constraints gate JUDGE-G1 read back by Harriet in a separate context), search plus transcript readback (deleted_and_expired legs 1-4, timer_changes leg 2, sent_once Part A, search_and_transcript), the mentions list (wall_mentions_and_links, edits Part B), a real restart readback (persistence step c vs leg 1), and refusal replays paired with an eligible success in the same criterion and then a re-read (functional prompt.md lines 48-52; e.g. hold_scope legs 1/3, timer_changes leg 5, edits leg 3 with the current version supplied so that only authorship can explain a refusal). Signed-out and walled read replays (signin Part A, wall_every_route leg 3) are confidentiality checks on returned content, which is a legitimate observable. They are not response-shape assertions. No criterion asks for a source read; the edits leg 3 version marker comes from recorded network traffic. Conditional legs are explicit, not 'looks right': the earlier-versions request in timer_changes and the suggestion request in mentions Part B. Probes are distinctive: 0 'JUDGE' hits in seed_data.json, app.js, index.html and server.js. Seeded anchors are unique (K-10 at exactly 7 days vs K-11 1 s younger; held K-17 overdue for release; 'heads of terms'/'Fenwick' only in M-12). The C/A/B order probe is deliberately non-alphabetical, and the %/_/* search probes come with near-miss controls (Q2/Q4/Q6). Requests are recorded and replayed within the same criterion, which matches individual mode (functional judge.toml mode='individual'). Feasibility evidence: the scripted Playwright golden (raw-evidence-index hashes verified; functional-before/after.json) performed every functional and polish criterion's steps and they PASSed, including measured thread scrollTop for live_updates and a real restart. This is scripted evidence only, not a configured judge run. Notes, not defects: (1) In live_updates_keep_my_work, the scroll baseline is noted before the reply box is opened. A judge that has to scroll to reach 'Draft will sent for your review.' could compare against a stale baseline. Wording that says to note the top-of-view right before Harriet's changes would remove the ambiguity. (2) persistence step c 'Sian gets not-available for M-11' leaves the route open (transcript or link address). Before and after use the same observable, so the result is still decidable. (3) The visual likert anchors ('calm', 'comfortable reading width') are inherently subjective craft judgements; the skill accepts likert anchors for craft (row 41). No configured LLM judge run on these bytes exists. That leaves judge consistency unmeasured, but it is not a demonstrated decidability defect.
